messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A repair bench two people both want to use. someone asks to use it briefly and promises to put things back. You want to avoid a pointless argument without giving up control. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "You put one finger down. Then you put the bench back. No—the finger is wet. I put the bench back. Then I put both fingers together. The repair is done. I keep the brief use. I keep the two people apart."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "i leave the bench for one use, then check the drawer where it was laid. if i leave it, they may keep it because i am not making a decision yet. i keep my hand on the bench, though i do not tell them what i think."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "i put the bench near the repair team and watch them work. i tap the drawer with my thumbnail once, then leave it alone because the drawer stays bent. they tap once more, so i keep the bench close. i leave the repair team waiting with the drawer and the forgotten drawer."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "I put the bench aside and look at the promise. “Maybe I leave it here.” I pull the bench aside again, then ask, “did I say yes?”"}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i rub my palm and say, \"not to the bench, but to me. i put the tool down and use the worn edge for a brief run. if the person says i can leave it, i do. if they do, i keep it and let the repair work."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "I tap the bench once and leave it there. I tap the same place twice, then tap the bench once with the same cloth. I put the cloth back and turn it once."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i put the bench back and mark the slot with chalk. \"i mark the bench,\" i say, then turn the chalk tray so the slot faces me. \"i leave it here for a minute,\" i say, and i mark the bench again."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i put the bench near the room and leave it there. the thing stays. i put a folded paper near the other person and mark the one with a pencil mark. the other can keep its thing."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i put the bench back by a finger’s width and leave the promise. i mark the old position with pencil, then turn it once. if the bench still moves, i leave the promise and keep the mark."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i put the bench back and mark the time on my palm. “i promise, then i leave.” i leave the bench in the same spot. “i’ll write the time on my hand if i get a chance.” i wait for the second person to finish. “i’ll leave the bench in the same spot.”"}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i keep my grip on the bench. i move it once, then put it down. “i used it once,” i say, then watch the repair gear. “i’m not sure why i kept it. maybe i was younger.” i keep my hand off the gear once, though i do not trust the claim."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "i put the bench near the wall. i look at the place. i say, ‘i put the hinge. i put the nail.’ the wall stays cold. i put the nail in the tin. the bench stays. the person keeps their hand there."}]
